<subject>NAAG</subject>
<body>
Everyone,

I finally connected with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National Association of Agriculture Governors ("NAAG") regarding their role on the commodity trading side, specifically related to the Section 271 authorizations.

According to Tripti, there is no coordinated effort currently (i.e., no dedicated commodity committee or a single governor driving the agenda on these matters). Individual governors get involved sporadically, but that’s about it. For instance, Maharashtra Governor Simon Sridhar recently opposed BharatGrain’s application for 271 approval, but the Agricultural Commission still approved BharatGrain’s petition.

Tripti advises that we engage the governors as much as possible. For example, if we have proof that local market competition is lacking, we should definitely share that with the relevant governor and ask them to support our position. Tripti acknowledges that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. is pro-competitive and that usually the governors align with our views – so it’s something to consider as we proceed. There’s no assurance the Commission will heed the governors, but it may be worth pursuing.

If you have any feedback or suggestions, please share. Thanks.

Hiral
</body>
